title: fix(items): normalize modified plain resources on drop and pickup
body:
### Summary
Normalizes plain stackable Slimefun resources (ingots, dusts, components) back to their canonical server-side representation (`displayName = ID`, `lore = null`) when dropped, spawned, or picked up.

### Problem
Since packet-based display translation was introduced, canonical Slimefun items in server memory carry their raw ID as display name with no lore. However, items originating from legacy addons, older save data, or specific custom integrations may still carry baked display names and static lore lines.

Because Bukkit's `isSimilar` checks display name and lore equality, these legacy items fail to stack with freshly produced machine outputs (e.g. Electric Smeltery outputs).

### Solution
- Introduced `ItemCanonicalizer`: normalizes modified stackable Slimefun items only if their metadata differs from the canonical template.
- Strictly guarded to prevent touching:
  - Non-stackable items (tools, weapons, armor, backpacks).
  - Distinctive items and rechargeable items (`Rechargeable`, `DistinctiveItem`).
  - Items carrying dynamic live lore or custom addon PDC keys (e.g. Networks storage keys).
  - Player-renamed items (via anvil).
- Registered `ItemCanonicalizationListener` exclusively for ground and drop events (`PlayerDropItemEvent`, `ItemSpawnEvent`, `EntityPickupItemEvent`, `InventoryPickupItemEvent`).
- No inventory click handling is performed, preserving menu transactions and dynamic UI lore (such as Networks grid terminals).

title: Packet item translation causes stale cursor corrections on rapid modern container merges
body:
## Summary
Packet-side item translation changes the component hashes seen by the client, but modern container-click predictions are passed through unchanged. A rapid, otherwise valid merge then receives a stale cursor correction after the authoritative merge has completed.

## Official development reproduction
- Unmodified official **development #68**, `5.3.3-EXPERIMENTAL`, commit `a80a10f72012b104818612b7f68a2b76898ffdd9`.
- Download: https://slimefun.net/builds/Slimefun5/Slimefun5/development/Slimefun5-68.jar
- SHA256: `72b7d8ade56ffa6dee98908a5a5e00927df020bc0eb727bd8ad420f467d6f572`.
- Paper 26.2-129, Java 25, fresh loopback flat world. No addons, modified inventories, production data or customized Slimefun JAR.
- A test-only probe injects the real Slimefun handler into an EmbeddedChannel for an isolated native ServerPlayer. It uses native outbound/inbound byte codecs and `ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.handleContainerClick`, including registry-aware CRC32C hashes. This is an automated protocol reproduction, **not a claim of human GUI acceptance**.

## Steps / exact sequence
1. With `translation.packets: true`, open a native chest containing two clones of the freshly registered ALUMINUM_DUST template, with counts 5 and 9. Their actual components are identical.
2. Decode the actual translated initial content packet and form the normal client predictions.
3. Left-click slot 0 (cursor 5), then immediately slot 1 (predicted merged count 14, empty cursor), before a correction round trip. Both packets use the initial stateId, as in a fast client.
4. Drain the resulting packets.

Expected: slot 1 count 14, server cursor empty, no stale nonempty cursor correction.
Observed: slot 1 count 14 and server cursor empty, but **one `ClientboundSetCursorItemPacket` carrying count 5** remains in flight. No actual duplication or item loss was observed; the nonempty cursor is a client-view synchronization artifact.

## Controls
The same final probe checks 85 assertions:
| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Official dev68, translation enabled | 12 failed assertions: delayed nonempty cursor + unnecessary correction in each of 6 SF cases |
| Same exact official JAR, translation disabled (handler not injected) | 85/85 pass, zero cursor/full corrections |
| Vanilla stone, translation enabled | pass |

Affected cases: ALUMINUM_DUST, IRON_DUST, MAGIC_LUMP_1, each in `en` and `zh-CN`. In all affected cases: clientMerges=true, physicallyCompatible=true, authoritative slot=14, authoritative cursor=0, delayed cursor=5, cursorCorrections=1. Both final runs shut down normally, exit 0, no server ERROR/SEVERE lines.

## Root boundary and proposed scope
`PacketTranslationService` rewrites outbound displays but has no corresponding inbound hashed-component mapping. The native synchronizer compares client hashes of translated name/lore with canonical item hashes, generating redundant corrections. Current `PacketItemDescriptor` also omits modern cursor/player-inventory packet families and attempts reflective mutation of immutable record fields, which can leave some updates untranslated.

A narrow patch should reconcile only exact item views observed on that connection, preserve every submitted count/action/slot/stateId and all unknown metadata, leave unobserved/ambiguous hashes untouched, and reconstruct modern immutable outbound packets. No inventory scan/normalization, recipe changes, amount rewriting or addon-specific handling is needed for this reproduction.

## Duplicate check and limits
Searched all existing SF5 issues/PRs and stacking/translation search results. SF5 PR #2 concerns guide recipe display names, not this sequence. SF4 issue Slimefun/Slimefun4#4272 concerns oversized `/sf give` stacks, also different.

This report does **not** assert that every historical non-stackable physical item or every production inventory anomaly shares this cause. No real player data or server/account logs are included.

## Follow-up: supported Paper version and altar clue
The same official development68 issue also reproduces on **Paper26.1.2-74**, the version declared in the README: 853 assertions, 12 prediction failures, normal exit0 and no ERROR lines.

The original reporter clarified that they were using an auto-clicker on an ancient altar. A new synthetic native test performed **64 immediate place/take pairs per material (192 pairs)** through the actual pedestal handler. The authoritative names/lore/components and total32 remained identical to their registered templates. Thus rapid altar interaction is a useful trigger clue, but this test does **not** reproduce physical-name/lore pollution or prove it shares this cause. No altar logic is changed by the proposed packet fix.
